title: Privacy versus the public's right to know
news: News publishers have challenged the data protection law for requiring a person's consent before journalists process their data.
syllabus: Information sharing and transparency in government · Ethical issues in media
link: Respect for individual privacy must be weighed against the public's right to know about matters of public interest.
question: As an editor, you hold verified evidence of a senior official's misuse of public funds, but he invokes his privacy and refuses consent. What will you do and why?

title: Turf versus national interest
news: Seven years on, India's services still argue over theatre commands, each guarding its turf.
syllabus: Leadership · Ethical dilemmas in government institutions
link: Institutional loyalty can override national interest; leaders must rise above turf to decide.
question: 'Shelving hard decisions is the least ethical course.' Discuss with reference to institutional reform in government.

title: Sentencing and objectivity
news: Two experts show that similar offenders get very different sentences depending on the judge, and propose a Sentencing Council.
link: Objectivity means like cases treated alike, on law and evidence, not personal views; guidelines make discretion accountable.
question: Discretion is essential in administration, yet it can become arbitrary. How can objectivity be ensured in discretionary decisions? Illustrate with an example.

title: When police become debt collectors
news: With civil suits taking years, influential creditors press police to turn money disputes into criminal cases.
syllabus: Probity in governance · Integrity, impartiality and non-partisanship
link: Discretion used for a powerful private party is abuse of power, even when the law is technically invoked.
question: As an SHO, an influential businessman asks you to register a cheating case against a borrower in what is clearly a civil dispute. What will you do and why?
